ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 and the AML/CFT Code of Practice 2018: all UBOs, directors, signatories, counterparties and ultimate beneficiaries must be screened against (i) the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list, (ii) the New Zealand designated terrorist and associated entities list under the Terrorism Suppression Act 2002, (iii) the New Zealand Russia Sanctions Act 2022 designations, (iv) the United States OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Consolidated Sanctions lists given the Swift LC and USD-clearing rails, (v) the United Kingdom HM Treasury consolidated sanctions list, and (vi) the European Union consolidated sanctions list. Domestic PEPs, foreign PEPs and international-organisation PEPs are identified under the AML/CFT Act 2009 using a licensed commercial PEP database. Screening is performed at onboarding, refreshed on every new LC issuance or payment instruction, and on a minimum six-monthly event-triggered basis.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Register, NZ Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment — online name availability search and reservation at https://companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must use Latin-alphabet characters; English and te reo Maori names are permissible, with Maori macrons accepted. Non-Latin-script foreign trading names must be transliterated into Latin characters for the statutory register, and any foreign-language trading name must be accurately transliterated and filed as an alternate name with the Companies Office. The name must not be identical or falsely 'too similar' to any existing or reserved name on the register. The suffix 'Limited' or an approved abbreviation is mandatory for a limited liability company unless a statutory exemption is obtained.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Anzac (protected under the Flags, Emblems, and Names Protection Act 1981)

International Company (internal client designator; the registered New Zealand name should use a descriptive equivalent such as 'International Trading' or 'IC Trading' to avoid confusion with a Cook Islands International Company)
Petrochemical (permissible only as a descriptive token where it does not imply state licensing or Crown endorsement)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The New Zealand Companies Office reserves an approved company name for 20 working days from the date of approval. An extension may be obtained by filing a fresh reservation before expiry, but repeated refiling is at the discretion of the Registrar. On refusal under section 22 of the Companies Act 1993, the applicant may, within 15 working days of the notice of refusal, file a written request for reconsideration with the Registrar of Companies stating the grounds of appeal and any permissible alternative name variant. If the Registrar maintains the refusal, the applicant may apply to the High Court of New Zealand for judicial review under the Judicial Review Procedure Act 2016 within 28 days of the decision. A new name application may be filed at any time without penalty.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Partial permissibility. Under section 189 of the Companies Act 1993, the registered office must be a physical address in New Zealand, open to the public for statutory hours, and available for service of process and statutory mail. A serviced-office provider with a genuine physical address, mail handling capability and inspection compliance is acceptable. A purely virtual address, PO Box or non-addressable location is prohibited. For an ISIC 4669 wholesale petrochemical distribution vehicle classified as Medium_Risk_Enhanced under AML/CFT, absence of local decision-making personnel, accounting records, bank account substance and contractual functions will attract enhanced supervisory scrutiny by the Registrar, the Inland Revenue Department and the Department of Internal Affairs.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk assessment: Medium-High. For a newly incorporated wholesale petrochemical trading entity using a serviced address, the estimated probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection within the first 12 months is 25-35%. The Companies Office conducts targeted compliance visits, the Department of Internal Affairs exercises inspection powers under the AML/CFT Act 2009, and the Inland Revenue Department may undertake premises visits under the Tax Administration Act 1994.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (No 105 of 1993), Sections 12-18 (incorporation and registration), Section 16 (name requirements), Section 17 (registered office), Section 152 (director requirements), Section 180 (first board resolutions); Companies (Incorporation and Company Documents) Regulations 1993.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, a business unit of the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), Wellington, New Zealand.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of a Company (Form NZCO - Company Registration), filed electronically through the New Zealand Companies Office online register.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up share capital is imposed by the Companies Act 1993. A company may issue shares for nil consideration or nominal value. There is no escrow account requirement for standard incorporation, although commercial AML/CFT or bank credit facilities may necessitate paid-up capital consistent with the business plan.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTIONS OF THE SOLE INCORPORATOR AND FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] LIMITED (the 'Company'), adopted under sections 122 and 180 of the Companies Act 1993. RESOLVED: (1) That the Company be incorporated as a company limited by shares pursuant to section 12 of the Companies Act 1993, with the name '[COMPANY NAME] LIMITED'. (2) That the authorized share capital of the Company be NZ$[X] divided into [Y] ordinary shares of NZ$[Z] each, and that the subscriptions set out in the register of shareholders are accepted; the shares are issued fully paid. (3) That the registered office of the Company be established at [New Zealand physical street address], and that the secretary if any be directed to file the registered office address with the New Zealand Companies Office. (4) That [Director Full Name] be and is hereby appointed as a director of the Company, and [Officer Full Name] be appointed as Chief Financial Officer and authorised signing officer, each to act until replaced by mutual resolution. (5) That the directors be and are hereby authorised to execute all documents, open all bank accounts, and make all filings necessary to register the Company with Inland Revenue, obtain an IRD number, register for GST if required, and secure all applicable licences and permits.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company name reservability and availability review
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office online register (www.companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The proposed company name must be checked for availability and compliance with section 16 of the Companies Act 1993, including the requirement to end with 'Limited' or 'Tapui' unless an exemption applies. Submit a name check or reserve the name through the online portal with supporting search results.
required_dossiers: Statement that the name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name
Consent of the proposed shareholder to use the name
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, the applicant may submit an alternative name or apply for review by the Registrar within ten working days, providing evidence that the name is not misleading.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of constitutional documents and consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office / Registered legal advisor or chartered accountant
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The company may operate under the Companies Act 1993 default rules or adopt a constitution. If a constitution is adopted, it must be signed by the shareholder(s) and filed with the application. Ensure express consent to act as director and shareholder is obtained in writing.
required_dossiers: Consent to act as director (Form RD2 or statutory declaration)
Address of registered office in New Zealand
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the documents are queried, correct any inconsistencies, re-execute the relevant consents, and resubmit within five working days under the Companies Act 1993.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of incorporation application to New Zealand Companies Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the completed Application for Registration of a Company electronically through the Companies Office digital gateway. Provide the proposed company name, registered office physical address (a residential or commercial address in New Zealand, not a PO Box), director details (at least one director resident in New Zealand or an Australian resident falling within section 152), shareholders' details, and the constitution. Pay the applicable filing fee online.
required_dossiers: Director's full name, address, and date of birth
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried or rejected, the applicant must cure the defect by responding to the query through the portal, amending the relevant details, and paying any additional fee. The Registrar will continue processing once compliance is established.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and New Zealand Business Number (NZBN)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, the New Zealand Companies Office registers the company and issues a Certificate of Incorporation. The New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) is automatically generated and assigned to the company at this stage. The certificate should be downloaded and retained for all subsequent licensing and banking procedures.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is not issued or the NZBN is not generated, contact the Companies Office helpdesk and provide the application reference number to request re-issuance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (Te Tari Taake) via myIR portal and IRD eServices; company registry through the New Zealand Companies Office and NZBN.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity that is not incorporated in New Zealand applies to Inland Revenue for a non-resident IRD number using form IR742 (Non-Resident Company IRD Application). If the entity is incorporated in New Zealand, it must first obtain a New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) from the Companies Office and then apply for an IRD number using form IR596 or through myIR. After the IRD number is issued, the entity must separately register for Goods and Services Tax (GST) if it carries on a taxable activity in New Zealand and its annual taxable supplies exceed NZD 60,000, or it may voluntarily register using form IR372, which can be filed online through myIR. No statutory trade license is required for wholesale distribution of virgin polyethylene and polypropylene granules.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone — a non-resident International Company that does not carry on a taxable activity in New Zealand and earns only non-New Zealand-source income is outside the New Zealand income tax net and has no GST registration nexus. If the entity becomes a New Zealand tax resident or begins substantial New Zealand-source trading, it would instead fall under Entity_Level_Taxation and become subject to NZ corporate income tax and GST on NZ taxable supplies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand does not operate a check-the-box system. Eligible closely-held companies may elect Look-Through Company (LTC) status under the Income Tax Act 2007, subpart HB, enabling pass-through of NZ-source income and losses. GST grouping elections and voluntary GST registration for zero-rated export traders are available under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985. Hybrid mismatch outcomes are mandatory and are not elective; no domestic hybrid mismatch election exists.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/Value Added Tax (Goods and Services Tax Act 1985)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 of taxable supplies in any 12-month period; voluntary registration is permitted for entities making only zero-rated export supplies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand has no statutory real-time fiscal clearance, mandatory e-invoicing, or digital stamping regime. Inland Revenue accepts GST returns and payments through myIR, and voluntary e-invoicing using the Peppol framework is permitted. Entities must retain source documents and export evidence in New Zealand for seven years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A supply of bulk polyethylene and polypropylene granules is zero-rated for New Zealand GST if the supplier exports the goods physically from New Zealand within 28 days of supply, or if the goods are supplied to a non-resident customer outside New Zealand and title passes outside New Zealand pursuant to a contract of sale or export. Offshore services and remote services supplied to non-resident buyers outside New Zealand may also be zero-rated. The exporter must hold contemporaneous commercial and customs evidence sufficient to establish actual export, foreign destination, and the export nature of the supply. Refunds of attributable input GST on zero-rated exports are claimed through normal GST returns subject to retention of complete export documentation.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (New Zealand Trade Single Window / CUSMED export entry)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical export of the PE/PP granules
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT bank credit advice evidencing receipt of export sale proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Inland Revenue may scrutinize zero-rated export claims by matching GST returns with customs export declarations and bank receipts. The burden lies on the supplier to prove the goods were exported; failure to do so results in a reassessment at 15% GST with interest from the original supply date. Shortfall penalties range from 20% for failing to take reasonable care, 20% for taking an unacceptable tax position, 50% for abusive tax position, and up to 150% for evasion. The 180-day foreign-currency repatriation period is a standard compliance and AML benchmark; while New Zealand legislation does not impose an absolute 180-day export-proceeds deadline, absence of inward remittance evidence within that period materially increases the risk of an audit adjustment or clawback.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua) — the sole central bank and monetary authority of New Zealand. There is no separate foreign exchange control administration, and the Reserve Bank does not issue exchange control permits, surrender certificates, or currency licenses. Its foreign-exchange mandate is confined to the management of official overseas reserves and the prudential supervision of banks and non-bank deposit takers under the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 2021. The operational oversight of cross-border payment reporting and anti-money laundering conduct rests with the joint AML/CFT supervisors: the Reserve Bank, the Financial Markets Authority, and the Department of Internal Affairs.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The New Zealand dollar (NZD) is a free-floating and fully convertible currency. New Zealand has accepted Article VIII obligations under the IMF Articles of Agreement, so current-account payments and transfers, including trade settlement, service fees, royalties, and profit remittances, are free from exchange restrictions. Capital-account convertibility is also open: no prior purchase, use, or repatriation authorization is required for equity injections, intercompany loans, dividend distributions, or liquidation proceeds moving through a New Zealand bank. The only material hurdles are not exchange controls but overlays in the investment and tax regimes: (i) the Overseas Investment Act 2005 requires consent for non-resident acquisitions of sensitive land or significant business assets (transaction value at or above the relevant monetary threshold of NZD 100 million for most business assets, with separate criteria for strategic and farmland transactions); and (ii) New Zealand source dividends, interest, and royalties paid to non-residents attract non-resident withholding tax, with statutory maxima up to 30% on dividends and 15% on interest and royalties, subject to treaty reduction and the approved issuer levy (AIL) alternative at 2% for interest. A tax-exempt International Company structured as a non-resident treasury vehicle must nevertheless document the source of each funded asset to avoid a deemed New Zealand stamping charge from the IRD.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: New Zealand imposes no mandatory surrender, repatriation, or conversion regime for export proceeds. There is no statutory timeline requiring an exporter to bring receipts onshore, and there is no compulsory conversion ratio into NZD. Foreign-currency export receivables may be retained indefinitely in offshore or New Zealand bank accounts. The only compliance frictions are (i) the AML/CFT record-keeping and suspicious-transaction reporting duties of the paying bank for international wire transfers, (ii) the financial arrangements rules of the Income Tax Act 2007, which can tax foreign-exchange movements for New Zealand resident companies, and (iii) the requirement that a New Zealand-registered bank classify any large unexplained inward credit as an 'unusual transaction' report under the AML/CFT Act 2009. For a tax-exempt International Company holding a Cook Islands or similar offshore incorporation, export proceeds can remain outside the New Zealand tax net provided no New Zealand permanent establishment is created and the proceeds are not derived through a New Zealand fixed place of business.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Tier-1 Capital Escrow Account (NZD/USD multi-currency) and Operational Current Account with SWIFT netting
Operational Trade Account (NZD) with Trade Finance and LC Ornamentation Window
Wholesale Trading and FX Hedging Account with dedicated Commodities Desk
Current Account for hydrocarbon wholesale settlement and Irrevocable Documentary Credit issuing facility
Domestic Working Capital Account restricted to NZD clearing; no offshore LC appetite for an exempt IC

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Low as a primary bank, Medium as an ancillary payment overlay. New Zealand does not maintain a dedicated e-money institution (EMI) license class. An offshore digital EMI (e.g. a United Kingdom or Singapore licensed payment institution) cannot operate as a settlement bank in New Zealand or issue NZD clearing instruments without registering on the Financial Service Providers Register and becoming a reporting entity under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009. For this International Company, a locally incorporated Tier-1 New Zealand bank remains mandatory for LC issuance, GST pooling, NZD settlement, and RBNZ-cleared high-value payments. The offshore EMI may be engaged solely as an FX execution and disbursement overlay, provided the EMI’s home license is verified, the underlying nostro settlement agent is not a shell bank, and every converted leg is supported by the commercial polymer supply contract; otherwise, correspondent banks will reject the wire.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: New Zealand law does not impose a statutory requirement for directors to appear physically at a bank branch. In current Tier-1 bank practice, a live audio-visual interview with at least one director and a designated account signatory is mandatory, and a physical branch visit is conditionally required only where the ultimate beneficial owner is a politically exposed person, the entity lacks a registered office in New Zealand, or sanctions screening produces an elevated risk score. Remote onboarding is accepted by ANZ, ASB, BNZ, and Westpac when the entity presents (i) a certificated certificate of incorporation, (ii) a recently dated certificate of good standing, (iii) apostilled constitutional documents, and (iv) director identification that can be verified by bank-grade digital KYC systems. For a Cook Islands International Company, New Zealand banks will insist that the entity first file an overseas company registration under the Companies Act 1993 if a place of business is established in New Zealand; the account may then be opened remotely for the overseas branch structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-exempt offshore International Company with no local employees or physical office seeking a full-service operating account in the name of a petrochemical trading entity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Certified true copies of the certificate of incorporation, constitution, directorship register, and register of charges; (2) overseas company registration under Part 18/19 of the Companies Act 1993 if New Zealand business is conducted; (3) an independent legal opinion from New Zealand counsel confirming the tax-exempt status, legal existence, and non-resident ownership structure; (4) a complete beneficial-ownership map to natural persons with passport and proof-of-address documents; (5) an audited or management-projected balance sheet evidencing the legitimate source of startup capital; and (6) a board resolution appointing the New Zealand bank as the principal clearing bank for the ISIC 4669 wholesale polymer distribution mandate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High projected monthly turnover (up to NZD 50 million equivalent) against a minimal physical office footprint, creating a scale versus substance mismatch.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Executed master supply agreements with virgin polyethylene and polypropylene producers; (2) underlying UCP600-form pro forma invoices from ECE suppliers; (3) warehouse receipts, vessel nomination lists, and cargo manifests evidencing stored polymer inventory; (4) a presentation to the bank trade finance committee of the complete goods-flow matrix; and (5) letters of intent or contractual offtake agreements from Asia-Pacific wholesale distributors proving the commercial substance of the proposed turnover.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: No previous bank relationship and inbound funding sourced from a tax-haven jurisdiction or from an unrelated third-party payer rather than the declared shareholder.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Unredacted intercompany loan agreements, share subscription documents, or tripartite payment delegation letters; (2) source-of-wealth and source-of-funds files for the promoting shareholder, including three years of bank statements; (3) a legal undertaking from the International Company stating that all LC drawdowns will be matched to underlying polymer purchase contracts; (4) a transaction-flow diagram screened against the sanctions lists administered by the New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade; and (5) a formal opinion on the applicability of the Overseas Investment Act 2005 to the capital injection.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Polymer inbound shipments routed through jurisdictions subject to enhanced due diligence or trade sanctions; dual-use or customs-integrity concerns on resin classifications.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) End-user declarations and destination control letters for each shipment; (2) producer mill test certificates and tonnage certificates for each polymer grade; (3) vessel screening results based on IMO numbers, B/L consignee names, and ISBP-appraised documentation; (4) a documented internal sanctions matrix confirming that all counterparties, banks, and shipping lines are absent from the United Nations, United States, United Kingdom, European Union, and New Zealand Consolidated Lists; and (5) an independent trade-counsel confirmatory memorandum for every trans-shipment route.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound shareholder equity contributions, intercompany loans, and trade pre-payments are cleared via SWIFT MT103 (outright) or MT202 (cover through an intermediate correspondent) to the International Company’s NZD or USD account at a Reserve Bank-regulated New Zealand bank. The payment narrative must state the economic purpose using clear wording such as 'Shareholder equity contribution', 'Intercompany loan — IC treasury line', or 'Prepayment for polyethylene granules under Contract No. X'. The Reserve Bank does not prescribe a national purpose-code tariff, but the receiving bank must record the purpose narrative and verify the sender’s bank authorization, the source-of-funds documentation, and the direct or indirect ownership chain. If the injected capital is used to acquire significant New Zealand business assets or sensitive land, an Overseas Investment Act 2005 consent number must be quoted in the supporting memorandum. International wire transfers are retained for record-keeping under the AML/CFT Act 2009 and may trigger a suspicious-transaction report only if the funding source or the overseas debit/credit institution presents a sanctions or corruption risk. All capital injections should be accompanied by a directors’ resolution and an updated share register to pre-empt the bank’s beneficial-ownership questionnaire.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The standard clearing rails for settlement of bulk polymer purchases are (i) an irrevocable documentary letter of credit issued by the New Zealand Tier-1 bank in MT700 form under UCP600/ISBP 821, with the beneficiating producer or commodity trader negotiating against conforming documents (full set of ocean bills of lading, certificate of origin, commercial invoice, packing list, and quality certification); and (ii) direct telegraphic transfers via SWIFT MT103 for spot prepayments or balance settlements on open-account terms. The LC rail matches the target payment rails described as Swift_LC and Irrevocable_LC: the importer’s bank opens an irrevocable credit, advances cover under MT202 to the nominated paying bank, and settles documents on presentation. For smaller cargo legs, documentary collections (DP/DA) and Bank Payment Obligation structures under the ICC URBPO rules are acceptable alternatives. New Zealand imposes no exchange-control approval for outbound disbursements; however, the remitting bank is obligated to screen all beneficiaries and vessel parties against sanction lists, and where the payment exceeds a legislated threshold the bank must ensure the transaction is not a suspicious transaction. Payment instructions for LC drawings should carry the LC number, contract number, and the words 'NOT SUBJECT TO FINANCIAL SANCTIONS' as well as the final destination clause for the polymer cargo.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable outright FX forwards (fixed-date and window forwards) in NZD/USD, NZD/CNH, and NZD/EUR executed with the corporate’s licensed New Zealand bank under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement and Credit Support Annex; no underlying trade-invoice restriction applies to a treasury-sophisticated International Company.

Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted-currency payables such as CNY, INR, and KRW, entered into through a permitted dealer, provided that the notional amount is matched to actual polymer import invoices and the settlement proceeds are traceable to the underlying trade payable.

Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CIRS) or USD/NZD basis swaps used to lock the economic cost of long-term LC refinancing and to neutralize the foreign-currency exposure on the IC’s ongoing capital injection and dividend distribution flows, all subject to the RBNZ derivatives reporting framework and the Financial Markets Authority business-conduct standards.
